_: What the community site shows about this plugin that manifest.json has no field for. Nothing here is shipped to users and Obsidian never reads it — see docs/development.md#the-listing. This is the template's copy and deliberately lists every field, so `check:listing` reports each one as removable — `npm run init` trims it to the two lines a plugin actually fills in. Keys starting with _ are notes and are ignored; JSON has no comments and only these scripts read this file, so they live here rather than in a document nobody opens.
_tags: Up to 3, in the order they should appear on the listing — the form lets you drag them, so the order is a choice. `node obsidian-listing-tags` prints the 76 the site accepts; anything else makes the form refuse to save.
_pricing: free | paid | optional-payment. Defaults to free, which is also what a plugin with no payment of any kind is; delete this line unless it is something else.
_payment_description: Only shown when pricing is not free. One line on what is paid for and what is not — the listing has no room to explain a licence.
_long_desc: Up to 1000 characters. Optional: the listing already renders the repository's README below it, so this is worth writing only if the README's opening is a poor summary out of context.
_short_desc: NOT a field to fill in here. The site takes it from manifest.json's description, so a second copy would be a second thing to keep right. check-listing refuses it.
_icon: The listing badge: a lucide icon name and a hex background. Left null the site picks one, which is why every unset listing has a house on red. Set both or neither.
_screenshots: Uploaded through the form, not from here — the site stores images by id and there is no path that starts with a file. Two or three that show the plugin doing its job; the first is the card image in search results.
_private_source: The form can also point the listing at a private mirror of the source via a GitHub App. That is an authorisation, not a value, so it is not represented here.
